_about: FULLY DOCUMENTED EXAMPLE. Copy to expected.json and edit for your org.
Every block is optional: delete a block and its checks are skipped (reported as SKIP).
Values here describe what you BELIEVE is configured. The suite asserts reality matches.

meta.name: Acme Corp - Copilot governance baseline
meta.notes: Baseline for all engineering orgs. Change requires security sign-off.

scope._doc: Where the checks run. 'enterprise' is optional and needs enterprise admin scope on your token.

_doc: The runner uses the `gh` CLI. Required scopes:
read:org                -> org settings and policies
admin:org (read)        -> Copilot seat + policy detail
read:enterprise         -> enterprise policy block (optional)
repo                    -> repository-level settings
Run `gh auth status` first. Checks needing missing scopes report SKIP, not FAIL.
Copilot content exclusion prevents Copilot from using matching files as context
and disables completions inside them.
IMPORTANT: exclusion is enforced by the Copilot backend/clients, not by git.
So this suite tests it two ways:
1. CONFIG check  -> the rules exist and match what you expect (run_checks.py)
2. BEHAVIOR check -> Copilot actually refuses on a real file (cases/*.md)
Both are required. Config alone proves nothing about enforcement.

org_level._doc: Paths configured at Organization settings > Copilot > Content exclusion.

acme-engineering._forbid_doc: Set true to FAIL when extra patterns appear (drift detection). Set false to only require the expected set is present.

repo_level._doc: Paths from a repo's .github/copilot/content-exclusion.yml (repo admins can add, not remove, org rules).

_doc: Files the suite creates/expects so a human or agent can run the +ve / -ve behavioral cases.
must_be_excluded  -> Copilot MUST refuse to read / must not complete in these.
must_be_allowed   -> Copilot MUST work normally here. This is the negative control:
it catches over-broad patterns that silently break developers.
Organization settings > Copilot > Policies.
Allowed values per key: 'enabled' | 'disabled' | 'unconfigured' | 'enabled_for_all' etc.
Use the literal string the GitHub API returns; run with --dump to see live values.

acme-engineering._public_code_doc: 'block' = duplication detection ON. This is the control most orgs care about most.

enterprise_policies._doc: Requires read:enterprise. Skipped entirely if scope.enterprise is absent.

_doc: Seat hygiene checks. All thresholds optional.
max_inactive_days: FAIL if any assigned seat has been unused longer than this.

acme-engineering._require_doc: true asserts seats are NOT auto-assigned to every member (least privilege).

reporting._fail_on_doc: Add 'SKIP' to make missing scopes a hard failure in CI.
